chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh and another, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said:
I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “Indeed, some of our companions speak of compulsion, and some of them speak of capability.”
He said: So he said to me, “Write: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:”

“O son of Adam, by My will you became one who wills, and by My strength you fulfilled My obligations toward Me, and by My blessing you gained strength to disobey Me. I made you hearing and seeing. Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself. That is because I am worthier of your good deeds than you are, and you are worthier of your evil deeds than I am. And that is because I am not questioned concerning what I do, while they shall be questioned.”
I have arranged for you everything you wanted.

key_terms.الِاسْتِطَاعَةِ: capability; the human capacity by which actions are undertaken
key_terms.الْجَبْرِ: compulsion; the doctrine that human beings are forced in their acts
key_terms.بِمَشِيئَتِي: by My will; indicating that human volition exists under Allah’s will
key_terms.حَسَنَةٍ: a good deed or blessing attributed to Allah’s grace
key_terms.سَيِّئَةٍ: an evil deed or misfortune attributed to the human self
key_terms.فَرَائِضِي: My obligations; the divinely imposed duties owed to Allah
key_terms.لَا أُسْأَلُ عَمَّا أَفْعَلُ: I am not questioned about what I do; affirming Allah’s absolute sovereignty
key_terms.مَعْصِيَتِي: disobedience to Me; sinful opposition to Allah’s command

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the balance between Allah’s decree and human responsibility?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the question of divine decree and human capability by affirming that human willing and action occur through Allah’s power and blessing, while responsibility for evil remains with the human being. It reflects the Shia theological position rejecting absolute compulsion and affirming accountability under divine sovereignty.
